questions.answer_text: Subhas Chandra Bose is affectionately revered as 'Netaji', meaning Respected Leader.

questions.question: Did young Subhas love his country India?

options.A: Yes, he loved India deeply and defended its honor
options.B: No, he did not care about India
options.C: He only cared about sports
options.D: He wanted to leave India forever

questions.answer_text: Yes, young Subhas possessed deep patriotism and love for India.

questions.question: What famous slogan was given by Netaji to greet each other with patriotic pride?

options.A: Jai Hind
options.B: Good Morning
options.C: Hello World

questions.answer_text: Netaji popularized 'Jai Hind' (Victory to India) as a national salutation.

questions.question: Who was Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and when was he born?
questions.reference_answer: Subhas Chandra Bose was a great Indian freedom fighter born on 23rd January 1897 to Janaki Bose and Prabhavati Devi.

questions.question: What was the profession of Netaji's father, Janaki Bose?
questions.reference_answer: Janaki Bose was a well-reputed advocate who practiced law.

What British professor at Presidency College made insulting remarks against Indian students and India?

options.A: Professor Oaten
options.B: Professor Smith
options.C: Professor Brown

questions.answer_text: Professor E.F. Oaten made derogatory and anti-India comments that insulted Indian students.

questions.question: Where did Subhas Chandra Bose's fiery nationalist temperament first come to public light?

options.A: Presidency College, Kolkata
options.B: Cambridge University, England
options.C: High Court of Cuttack

questions.answer_text: His nationalist temperament first came to light during the student protests at Presidency College, Kolkata.

questions.question: Why did the students at Presidency College confront Professor Oaten?

options.A: Because he made rude, anti-India comments and insulted Indian national pride
options.B: Because he gave very difficult homework assignments
options.C: Because the college library closed too early
options.D: Because they wanted longer summer vacations

questions.answer_text: Students protested because Professor Oaten made discriminatory and offensive anti-India remarks.

questions.question: What does the word 'rusticated' mean in the context of Subhas's college life?

options.A: Expelled or suspended from the educational institution as a disciplinary punishment
options.B: Promoted to the next academic grade with honors
options.C: Sent on an overseas educational tour

questions.answer_text: Rustication meant being expelled or suspended from college by the British authorities.

questions.question: What does having a 'nationalist temperament' mean?

options.A: Having strong patriotism, love for one's motherland, and defending national self-respect
options.B: Traveling to many foreign countries for sightseeing
options.C: Collecting maps and geographical globes

questions.answer_text: A nationalist temperament represents intense patriotic devotion to one's nation and refusal to tolerate subjugation.

questions.question: How did young Subhas respond when he heard anti-India remarks from a British teacher?

options.A: He stood up bravely with his fellow students and protested against the insult
options.B: He remained silent and accepted the humiliation
options.C: He dropped out of school secretly
options.D: He agreed with the British teacher

questions.answer_text: He refused to accept disrespect toward India and boldly led the protest against the British professor.

questions.question: In what year was Subhas Chandra Bose born, and in which era did this incident occur?

options.A: Born in 1897 during British colonial rule in India
options.B: Born in 1947 after Indian independence
options.C: Born in 1857 during the First War of Independence
options.D: Born in 1914 during World War I

questions.answer_text: Subhas was born in 1897 and grew up when India was under British colonial domination.

questions.question: What qualities of leadership did Subhas Chandra Bose demonstrate even as a young college student?

options.A: Moral courage, standing up for fellow students, and uncompromising dignity
options.B: Indifference to student issues and seeking personal favor from authorities
options.C: Fear of authority and avoidance of difficult situations
options.D: Focusing solely on passing exams without caring about social reality

questions.answer_text: Young Subhas displayed fearless leadership, solidarity with fellow students, and dedication to justice.

questions.question: Explain what happened between Subhas Chandra Bose and Professor Oaten at Presidency College.
questions.reference_answer: At Presidency College in Kolkata, British Professor Oaten made offensive anti-India comments. Young Subhas and student protestors confronted him, leading to Subhas being rusticated from the college.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'nationalist temperament' and how did young Subhas demonstrate it?
questions.reference_answer: A nationalist temperament is a strong sense of patriotism and defense of one's motherland. Subhas showed this by refusing to tolerate colonial insults against India at Presidency College.

questions.question: Describe Netaji's family background and upbringing as introduced in the early life story.
questions.reference_answer: Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23rd January 1897 into an educated, distinguished family. His father Janaki Bose was a well-reputed advocate, and his mother was Prabhavati Devi.

Why was the confrontation at Presidency College in 1916 considered a pivotal turning point in Subhas Chandra Bose's life?

options.A: It transformed him from a promising academic student into a resolute, uncompromising leader of anti-colonial resistance
options.B: It made him decide to abandon public life and live quietly abroad
options.C: It caused him to accept British colonial dominance without question
options.D: It ended his interest in Indian politics and social justice

questions.answer_text: The incident proved that Subhas would never compromise Indian national dignity for personal career advancement, marking his emergence as a revolutionary leader.

questions.question: What systematic colonial attitude was reflected in Professor Oaten's behavior toward Indian students at Presidency College?

options.A: Racial superiority, imperial arrogance, and contempt for Indian cultural dignity
options.B: Democratic equality and mutual cultural respect
options.C: Support for Indian self-governance and student rights

questions.answer_text: Professor Oaten's remarks reflected the widespread racial prejudice and imperial superiority that characterized colonial administration in educational institutions.

questions.question: How did Subhas's decision to face rustication rather than apologize reflect his core political philosophy?

options.A: He believed national self-respect and the collective honor of India were paramount over individual comfort or academic degrees
options.B: He did not value education and wanted an excuse to leave college
options.C: He acted impulsively without understanding the consequences
options.D: He wanted to gain popularity solely for personal ambition

questions.answer_text: Subhas's refusal to surrender demonstrated his profound conviction that self-respect and resistance to oppression are non-negotiable principles.

questions.question: What broader socio-political impact did the Presidency College rustication have on the youth and student movements of Bengal?

options.A: It galvanized student political consciousness and established Subhas as a courageous youth icon against colonial tyranny
options.B: It discouraged students across Bengal from participating in any national causes
options.C: It caused all colleges in Bengal to shut down permanently
options.D: It made the British administration increase student scholarships

questions.answer_text: The incident electrified the student community across Bengal, proving that young Indians could fearlessly challenge colonial authority.

questions.question: In analyzing Subhas's character, how did his family background as the son of Janaki Bose, an advocate, interact with his rebellious national spirit?

options.A: Growing up in an intellectually rigorous and legally conscious home gave him a sharp sense of justice, rights, and ethical duty
options.B: It forced him to follow a conventional government career regardless of ethics
options.C: It isolated him from Indian societal issues
options.D: It caused him to reject all forms of legal reasoning and debate

questions.answer_text: His father's legal discipline and high moral standing provided an intellectual foundation for young Subhas's intense pursuit of justice and human dignity.

questions.question: Which of the following historical statements accurately describes the long-term culmination of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's nationalist struggle?

options.A: He later organized the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) and led an armed military liberation campaign for Indian freedom
options.B: He became a colonial civil servant and served the British empire until retirement
options.C: He gave up the freedom struggle and settled as an author in France
options.D: He accepted a hereditary title from the British monarch

questions.answer_text: Netaji went on to lead the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army), launching an unprecedented armed campaign to liberate India from British rule.

questions.question: How did Netaji's early moral stand against Professor Oaten foreshadow his later famous exhortation: 'Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom'?

options.A: Both manifested an uncompromising readiness for supreme personal sacrifice in exchange for absolute national freedom
options.B: Both were focused only on academic curriculum reform
options.C: Both emphasized accepting British compromises and concessions
options.D: There was no thematic connection between the two events

questions.answer_text: His early willingness to sacrifice his academic future for national dignity directly presaged his ultimate call for total national sacrifice for complete independence.

questions.question: Critically analyze how the rustication of Subhas Chandra Bose from Presidency College shaped his subsequent political trajectory as a revolutionary leader.
questions.reference_answer: Subhas's rustication from Presidency College in 1916 proved that he prioritized national dignity and anti-colonial justice above personal prestige. Confronting Professor Oaten's racist slurs galvanized his revolutionary resolve, cementing his status as an uncompromising youth leader dedicated to total Indian independence.

questions.question: Examine the moral conflict between colonial authority and student self-respect in the Presidency College incident.
questions.reference_answer: The incident highlighted the clash between imperial authority, which demanded passive obedience from colonized subjects, and the burgeoning national consciousness of Indian youth who demanded equal respect and human dignity. Subhas's resistance demonstrated that moral righteousness supersedes oppressive colonial regulations.

questions.question: Evaluate the role of Janaki Bose and Prabhavati Devi in fostering the values that characterized Netaji's fearless character.
questions.reference_answer: Janaki Bose's integrity as an eminent advocate instilled a profound respect for justice and ethics, while Prabhavati Devi's strong moral upbringing nurtured Subhas's spiritual strength and deep love for his people, preparing him for the hardships of the freedom movement.

questions.question: Synthesize the overarching lesson that contemporary youth can derive from Netaji's fearless defiance of imperial oppression.
questions.reference_answer: Netaji's defiance teaches modern youth to maintain uncompromising moral integrity, stand up courageously against injustice and discrimination, place national and community welfare above selfish interest, and uphold human dignity under all circumstances.

sequence_test.description: These questions test whether the learner understands the chronological sequence of Netaji's early life and student rebellion.

questions.question: What is the correct chronological sequence of events in young Netaji's early life?

options.A: Birth in 1897 -> Enrolling in Presidency College Kolkata -> Protest against Professor Oaten -> Rustication from College
options.B: Rustication -> Enrolling in College -> Birth in 1897 -> Protest
options.C: Protest -> Birth in 1897 -> Rustication -> Presidency College
options.D: Presidency College -> Rustication -> Birth in 1897 -> Protest

questions.answer_text: The timeline starts with Netaji's birth on 23rd January 1897, followed by his studies at Presidency College, the confrontation with Professor Oaten, and subsequent rustication.

questions.question: Arrange the developmental milestones of Subhas Chandra Bose's early journey:

options.A: Upbringing by Janaki Bose & Prabhavati Devi -> Emergence of Nationalist Temperament -> Defense of Indian Dignity -> Emergence as Youth Freedom Icon
options.B: Emergence as Youth Icon -> Birth -> Advocate Father -> College Protest
options.C: College Protest -> Upbringing -> Birth -> Nationalist Temperament
options.D: Nationalist Temperament -> Upbringing -> College Protest -> Birth

questions.answer_text: His values were nurtured by his parents, leading to his nationalist temperament, courageous defense of Indian pride, and emergence as an iconic leader.
